public_body: Cotuit Board Of Fire Commissioners Union Negotiation Committee
overall: The AG found the committee's May 22 executive session discussion was properly held, but violated the OML by giving an ambiguous notice purpose and by the chair failing to declare detriment to negotiations; remote participation claim rejected, non-OML issues declined; no remedial action ordered.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the May 22 executive session discussion about Inspector General concerns on the firefighter contract should have been held in open session.
allegations.key_passage: We therefore agree with the Committee that this discussion fell within the parameters of both Purposes 1 and 3 as a complaint against the Fire District which could have impacted the Committee's ongoing negotiations with the fire fighter's union.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the notice and meeting failed to identify the executive session purpose relied on; the topic 'Union Negotiations' was ambiguous.
allegations.key_passage: However, as stated, the notice topic was unclear as to which executive session purpose or purposes the Committee relied upon.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the committee failed to follow procedural requirements for convening in executive session, including the chair's required declaration.
allegations.key_passage: Furthermore, because the Committee relied, in part, on Purpose 3 for the executive session, the chair should have declared that having the discussion in open session would have been detrimental to the Committee's negotiating position.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged an individual (non-member counsel) was improperly allowed to participate remotely by telephone at the May 22 meeting.
allegations.key_passage: Because remote participation only applies to public body members, the Committee did not violate the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complaint also asserted the committee was not the proper body to negotiate for the fire district and asked when it hired counsel; both outside the OML.
allegations.key_passage: Both issues are outside of the Open Meeting Law and we thus decline to review them.
